newsitem.title: EGYPT: ARAFAT PUSHES "UNITING FOR PEACE" STEP AT U.N.
newsitem.headline: ARAFAT PUSHES "UNITING FOR PEACE" STEP AT U.N.

text.p: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat urged Arab states on Sunday to press on with plans for a special "uniting for peace" session of the General Assembly to bypass U.S. vetoes of Security Council resolutions critical of Israel.

The Arab group of states at the United Nations said last week it would request such a meeting after the United States twice blocked resolutions telling Israel to stop building houses for Jews in disputed East Jerusalem.

This calls for holding an emergency special session of the assembly 24 hours after receipt by the secretary-general of a request supported by at least nine of the 15 Security Council members or a simple majority of the 185-member assembly.
The Jewish housing project at Jabal Abu Ghneim, also known as Har Homa, has provoked a crisis in Israeli-Palestinian talks and 11 days of non-stop unrest in the West Bank.

Arab states are moving closer to a freeze on relations with the Jewish state and the campaign gathered pace as Arab foreign ministers met in Cairo on Sunday for their regular twice-yearly conference at Arab League headquarters.

Arafat, the guest of honour at the opening session, said Israel had declared war on the Palestinian people by surrounding Palestinian areas with tanks in response to Palestinians throwing stones in protest at the settlement.
He said the U.S. position on Jerusalem violated the letter of guarantee signed by former U.S. secretary of state James Baker at the historic Middle East conference in Madrid in 1991.
"I urge you to make an effort so that this ("uniting for peace") resolution can have an effect," he added.

The "uniting for peace" formula was originated by the United States to enable the assembly to act "if the Security Council, because of lack of unanimity of the permanent members, fails to exercise its primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security."

Arafat said: "Israel has refused to abide by what it has signed... Unfortunately the Israeli government has turned its back on the peace process. It has started with the most dangerous point (Jerusalem) in order to defy not only Palestinians but all Arab nation and the Islamic nation."

Arafat, president of the autonomous Palestinian Authority in Gaza and the West Bank, did not mention any other specific measures to tackle what Arabs see as U.S. and Israeli contempt for the commitments they have made in Middle East peace talks.
But some of the Arab ministers are talking openly of freezing ties with the Jewish state and reviving the old Arab boycott of Israel, which has partially collapsed.
Several of the ministers said earlier their countries were willing to go along with measures to isolate Israel.
Omani Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Youssef bin Alawi bin Abdullah, said Arabs would confront Israel's policies "until the Day of Judgement".
Oman, one of the few Gulf countries which has made overtures to Israel, froze ties with the Jewish state last week because of its settlement policy.
Arab League Secretary General Esmat Abdel-Meguid said Arabs must stand united to confront Israel's anti-peace policies.

"We must search our souls to review our positions and determine our work to confront this barabaric challenge and to stand up to Israel's defiance of the will and resolutions of the international community," Abdel-Meguid said in a speech.

"The United States provides protection for Israel through its veto in the Security Council. This raises many question marks and begs the question on America's role as a sponsor of the peace process," he said.
